scope: Editorial decisions for the seven route 3 follow-ups on new SSVEP frequencies: the reference-spectrum query (REF), the head and feature follow-up (REF2) with the two softmax heads, the phase jitter, the phase ramp, the CCA mechanism diagnostics, the CCA adapter and the transfer of the adapter models to Wearable-102. Its own manifest: it amends no earlier review and changes no released file. questions-in-language-update.json, deployment-topics.json and mvp.json keep their bytes; the follow-ups sit in their own file, new-ssvep-frequencies-update.json, on the new page /topics/new-ssvep-frequencies/. Every figure is read from the audited export of its study, pinned by SHA-256 here and bound by that study’s reviews and receipts, through the three block modules (blocks_query.py, blocks_phase.py, blocks_cca.py), which apply the declared edits and select named fields. Nothing was re-run: no model was loaded, no score recomputed and no network used.

approval.basis: The owner’s decision D1 in chat on 2026-10-19, recorded in owner-decisions.json: publish the seven SSVEP follow-ups (new-ssvep-frequencies). Each study’s research receipts approve an aggregate handoff and leave website publication to the site; publication on the site rests on D1. Defaults stated to the owner and not objected to: the thread is linked and the commenter is not named (D6); the cross-spectral round is a status card with no figures (D9); the adapter handoff binding (R1) and the phase wording (R5) were re-checked by independent reviewers in the publishing session (R1_R5). Local build only: no deployment, GitHub, Hugging Face or Zenodo action.
previewDefaults: Placement: a new question page, /topics/new-ssvep-frequencies/, in the adapting group after questions-in-language. The route 3 page keeps its bytes and gains one link with no figures.
Cards 1 to 6 share one scope line, the BETA cohort route 3 studied; card 7 has its own scope strip with the participant-overlap caveat and the A2 line on which CCA it reports.
Each card prints its own study’s interval: the hierarchical paired bootstrap with seed 20261007 for cards 1 to 4, the paired person bootstrap with seed 20261015 for cards 5 to 7.
The bet in the thread, that held-out accuracy would clear 39%, appears once, on card 4, from studies.phase_ramp.thread_bet; the threshold prints as the thread states it (R5 M5).
The commenter’s confidence figure is absent from the file, the page and this manifest (R5 M7).

Names: the plan’s name key, site names first and export codes second; one site name for the cropped-spectrum match of the diagnostics and adapter exports, and its own name for the Wearable-102 cropped-spectrum check.
Counts: one new question page; no new dataset, model or leaderboard row.
decisionsOfThisReview: Values: every level and contrast is its study export’s own double, through the block modules; units stay fractions. The export audit re-derives every figure from the pinned research files without the block modules.
Declared edits only: each is listed under declaredEdits and applied by the block modules, which refuse an edit that does not find what it names.
The one-vs-rest head (route 3’s B-sh) is cited, point and interval, from the live route 3 file, which keeps its bytes.
The adapter’s figures come from its export 6f68114e… only; the handoffs are context and never a copy source (R1).
Wearable-102: the A2 note names the CCA the transfer reports (three harmonics) beside the dry-versus-wet page’s (four harmonics) on the same windows.
Cohort, Wearable-102 scope and endpoints are read from the blocks and required equal across every study that states them; the core 40-way chance level is the core matrix’s BETA track value.

Credits: BETA’s released rights record from the route 3 file and its conditions from deployment-topics.json; the corrigendum from the REF2 phase table that its protocol pins; CBraMod’s licence from the core matrix’s model record; Wearable-102’s released record from deployment-topics.json, with the Readme and the consent scope from the readings.

releaseRecord.decision: Publish the seven route 3 follow-ups on new SSVEP frequencies as their audited aggregates, on a new question page, outside every leaderboard.
releaseRecord.rights: BETA keeps its released record: CC BY 4.0, cohort aggregates only, with participant consent described for noncommercial scientific research. Wearable-102 keeps its released record: CC BY 4.0, cohort aggregates only. The frozen CBraMod features are the ones route 3 used; no weights are distributed.
releaseRecord.researchRelease: Each study’s receipts approve an aggregate handoff and bind its export, protocol and reviews by SHA-256; website publication rests on the owner’s decision D1.
releaseRecord.binding: This record approves the served file the export audit names.

notPublished: Per-person, per-fold, per-rotation, per-seed, per-window and per-frequency values of any kind, predictions, scores, features, fitted heads and the sealed run files: only cohort levels, paired contrasts with their intervals, transition shares and check counts are published.

The handoffs, protocols, freezes, receipts, reviews and the canonical jitter score themselves: each is pinned by SHA-256 in the release manifest and checked by the export; several carry private storage paths.
The cross-spectral round: in progress at the freeze; its status card carries no figures, and it ships as its own file and release.
Measured compute: run times, memory and process identifiers.
The adapter’s per-seed accuracies and its CROP-RESIDUAL transitions; the Wearable-102 contrast against the cropped-spectrum check.
